To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the multinational can improve the level of backward linksages in the local market, but this improvement is not always in the best interest of the multinational.
the presence of a foreign multinational firm increases backward linkages when the domestic market is large and the domestic firms are relatively inefficient.
the presence of a multinationals leads to a technology transfers and modifies the degree of linkages in the economy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the multinational presence on backward linkages and technology transfer.
the impact of technology transfer on backward linkages.
the impact of the multinational's entry in a local economy and the technology transfer that it may bring about.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
technology transfer by multinationals can be an important factor in the creation of backward linkages and, consequently, a source of economic development.
, in general, the presence of multinationals in developing countries increases backward linkages in local firms.
the multinational can benefit from transferring technology to local suppliers when the local market is large and the local firms have a low level of technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multinational can increase the backward linkages when it enters the domestic economy and the local suppliers are not very productive.
the presence of multinationals in a domestic market may have a positive effect on backward linkages in that market.
backward linkages are not necessarily enhanced by the presence of multinationals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of multinationals in developing countries could be beneficial for the local economy.
the multinational's decision of technology transfer is a strategic one, as it can have a significant impact on the level of backward linkage and on the multinational's profits.
the presence of a foreign multinational in a local economy may not only lead to technology transfer but also increase backward linkages.
